summary:
Space mission design is notoriously complex, requiring continuous trade-offs between competing constraints—payload mass, power budgets, delta-v, communications, orbital dynamics, and financial reserves. For students, these interdependent concepts often remain theoretical and abstract. 

To bridge this gap, Project Kalpana Chawla created NASA AEROQUEST: an interactive, browser-based 3D mission design and flight simulation game. Inspired by NASA’s Mission Design Lab (MDL) and JPL’s Concept Maturity Level (CML 1–4) framework, the game enables individual students or collaborative teams of up to four (Mission Director, Payload Lead, Spacecraft Bus Engineer, Trajectory & Comms Officer) to take a mission from initial formulation to live flight operations.

Players select science objectives across diverse planetary scenarios (Moon, Europa, Earth, Deep Space), configure spacecraft components in an interactive 3D WebGL CAD hangar, balance real-world physics budgets (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, 1/R² solar flux drop-off, eclipse battery depth-of-discharge, DSN link budgets), and simulate flight ConOps with dynamic in-flight anomalies. 

By transforming static textbook equations into immediate visual cause-and-effect gameplay, our project demystifies systems engineering, empowering the next generation of aerospace explorers to master the trade-offs behind real spaceflight.
details:
### 1. What It Does and How It Works

NASA AEROQUEST guides players through the complete end-to-end lifecycle of a space mission:

1. **Mission Formulation (CML 1 & 2)**: Players select a real-world scientific destination (such as the Artemis Lunar South Pole, Europa Ocean Plume Explorer, or Earth Climate Sentinel) and review core scientific questions, environmental radiation levels, and thermal hazards.

2. **Interactive 3D Spacecraft Engineering (CML 3)**: In an interactive 3D WebGL CAD cleanroom, players equip instruments, power units (Deployable Solar, UltraFlex, or Plutonium-238 RTGs), propulsion thrusters, star trackers, and antenna systems. Players can activate an "EXPLODE CAD" mode to inspect internal structural packaging.

3. **Multi-Disciplinary Physics Engine**: Behind the scenes, every choice triggers coupled physics calculations:

- **Mass & Launch Matching**: Enforces NASA's 20% Mass Growth Allowance (MGA) against authentic booster payload curves (Electron, Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, SLS).

- **Power & Eclipse Modeling**: Simulates Inverse-Square solar drop-off ($1/R^2$) and computes battery Depth-of-Discharge (DoD) during orbital shadow to prevent spacecraft brownouts.

- **Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation**: Computes available $\Delta V = I_{sp} \cdot g_0 \cdot \ln(m_0 / m_f)$ against required orbital insertion burns.

- **RF Link Budget**: Computes Deep Space Network (DSN) and Near Space Network (NSN) link margins in dB to prevent onboard data recorder overflow.

4. **Flight ConOps Simulation & Dynamic Anomalies**: Players launch through a T-minus countdown sequence, monitor live orbital telemetry, and resolve real-time in-flight emergencies (solar particle storms, sensor brownouts, cryovolcanic plumes).

5. **Post-Mission Evaluation & Debrief**: Missions receive an authentic Systems Engineering letter grade (A+ to F) and a 1,000-point performance breakdown benchmarked against actual NASA missions (LRO, Europa Clipper, PACE, JWST).

---

### 2. 4-Player Team Collaboration

The game supports both solo play and a 4-seat concurrent engineering team mode reflecting real NASA engineering tables:

- **Mission Director (MD)**: Manages financial reserves, the 15% NASA contingency budget, and final Launch Readiness Review (LRR) Go/No-Go signoff.

- **Payload & Science Lead (PSL)**: Maximizes science points, monitors Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs), and matches instruments to science targets.

- **Spacecraft Bus & Power Engineer (SBSE)**: Governs structural dry mass, solar vs. RTG selection, battery DoD, and thermal shielding.

- **Trajectory & Communications Officer (TCO)**: Manages $\Delta V$ propellant margins, launch vehicle matching, and ground station link budgets.

---

### 3. Benefits & Intended Impact

- **Breaks Down Academic Silos**: Rather than learning orbital mechanics or circuit power in isolation, students see how adding a single instrument ripples across rocket selection, battery weight, and project budget.

- **Accessible STEM Education**: Runs natively in any modern web browser without downloads, VR headsets, or expensive licenses, making systems engineering education globally accessible to schools and universities.

- **Hands-On Failure Learning**: Students safely experience failure modes (battery exhaustion in eclipse, negative RF link budgets, structural chassis overload) and iterate to discover viable point designs.

---

### 4. Tools, Coding Languages, and Technologies

- **Frontend Core**: React 18, TypeScript, Vite.

- **3D Graphics & Shaders**: Three.js (WebGL procedural spacecraft CAD, orbital trajectory visualizer, celestial shadow terminators).

- **Styling & UI**: Tailwind CSS, Lucide React icons, Canvas Confetti.

- **Audio Synthesis**: Web Audio API (procedural NASA Quindar beeps, thruster rumble, telemetry clicks).

- **Deployment & CI/CD**: GitHub Pages and GitHub Actions.

---

### 5. Creativity & Innovation

- **"Explode CAD" Visual Inspection**: Bridges the gap between abstract numbers and physical spacecraft design by allowing players to physically dismount and inspect parts in real-time 3D.

- **Integrated Mission Segments**: Concurrently visualizes the Space Segment, Launch Segment, Ground Segment, and User Segment in one cohesive interface.

- **Dynamic In-Flight Narrative**: Transitions from an engineering tool into an adrenaline-fueled mission operations simulator with randomized, scientifically grounded anomalies.

---

### 6. Key Engineering Factors Considered

- **NASA JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4)** for progressive gate reviews.

- **NASA 20% Mass Growth Allowance (MGA)** flight certification rules.

- **Deep Space Network (DSN 34m/70m)** dish scheduling and distance path loss.

- **Congressional Budget Caps** and mandatory 15% financial contingency reserves.
